doc.title: Shelly Berg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: His father teaches him chords and the jazz records
summary: His father taught him chords starting with That's All, and sat him down with Tatum, Peterson, Evans, Powell and others to listen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well how did you make the transition from just playing what was on the page to expanding that, to comping and all that?

All right, well when I was about ten or eleven my dad, as I said, he was figuring out that this was somebody that he might be able to play tunes with some day. So he started showing me basic chords and — don’t ask me why, the first tune he taught me was “That’s All.”
That’s a bit of a challenge.

Yeah. Well he taught me the first three chords, basically playing up from F minor, G minor, A minor and just back down. And I did that for a while, then he taught me [scats], so my mother must have gone crazy for about two weeks, I just played that up and down the piano, the first four bars of “That’s All” until he finally taught me [scats], and I got that other chord, and that was the next couple of weeks. So it was a slow process. That was the beginning. As I said there was always music in the house. My dad, whenever he was home there was always a record on. He had a big, huge collection and so he was sitting me down with Art Tatum and Oscar Peterson, Bill Evans and Bud Powell and Red Garland and Cannonball Adderley and Milt Jackson, from an early age. down and saying, “Listen to this, what are you hearing,” and really just mentoring me along. And he still does.
